answer_raw:
Paris tops the 2026 quality‑of‑life rankings in both Monocle’s survey and City & Local’s Monocle‑derived list, with Perth also emerging as a standout city in the same survey [5][6].

The **EIU Global Liveability Index 2026** scores 173 cities on 30 indicators, giving an average score of **76.1/100** [1][2]. In that index, **Tokyo** ranks **10th** and **Osaka** **7th**; at the opposite end, **Tehran** falls to **164th** out of 173, entering the world’s ten least liveable cities [3][2].

Oxford Economics’ **Global Cities Index 2026** ranks 1,000 cities overall, with **New York** taking the top spot. However, when the index isolates the “quality of life” dimension, only **one U.S. city** appears in that subset, and no U.S. city dominates the quality‑of‑life rankings [4].

Business Insider’s 2026 Global Cities Index, built on Oxford Economics data, lists the top 20 cities for quality of life. The report notes that eight U.S. cities are in the overall top 20, but only **one** makes it into the quality‑of‑life subset [4].

Monocle’s 2026 Quality‑of‑Life survey, which evaluates safety, connectivity, governance, green space, and more, highlights **Paris** as a perennial leader and notes **Perth** as a rising contender, while North American cities struggle in areas such as crime and housing [6].

Numbeo’s Mid‑Year 2026 Quality‑of‑Life Index publishes a historical snapshot of many cities but does not single out any particular city in its current release [7].
